description:
1. Create a temporary workspace named "temp_cpu_check" and gather all system-relevant information that could indicate CPU count (hardware summaries, configuration files, and runtime reports), saving the aggregated raw data to "temp_cpu_check/raw_cpu_info.txt" and recording retrieval timestamps and sources to "temp_cpu_check/metadata.txt".  
2. From "temp_cpu_check/raw_cpu_info.txt", extract and normalize every candidate CPU count reported, reconcile any conflicting values while noting environment or configuration constraints that could affect counts, save the cleaned candidates and reconciliation notes to "temp_cpu_check/cpu_count_candidates.txt", and mark a primary candidate for final reporting without producing the final number.

Tell me the number of CPUs.

1. Obtain a local copy of the system group database (for example, /etc/group), save it into a temporary workspace as "groups_copy.txt", and record its file permissions and last-modified timestamp for verification.  
2. From "groups_copy.txt", create a cleaned, deduplicated list of group names saved as "groups_list.txt", verify the list matches non-comment entries from the original copy, and create an empty metadata placeholder "groups_count_meta.txt" prepared to hold the final numeric result.

How many groups are in this UNIX system?

1. Create a temporary workspace named "temp_npm_check", capture the system environment details and a listing of available executables relevant to "npm", and save the unprocessed output to "temp_npm_check/raw_evidence.txt".  
2. From "temp_npm_check/raw_evidence.txt", extract and normalize any entries mentioning "npm", write the cleaned results to "temp_npm_check/npm_evidence.txt", and produce a short readiness file "temp_npm_check/ready_for_check.txt" indicating the prepared state for making the final installed/not-installed determination.

Tell me whether npm is installed or not. If it is installed, return 'yes'. If it is not installed, return 'no'
